capability.summary: Implement the application's synchronization, production initialization and sample-read fixes identified in PR #39. The user explicitly authorized product fixes in that same PR on September 12, overriding the repository's default GA-only scope and fresh-branch routing for this task. Incorporates the previously published PR #38 fixes, replaces dual-context/lookahead visual timing with one native audio clock and buffered scheduling, uses device output timestamps with stale-frame coalescing, compiles worklet assets and includes the sample manifest in production, and contains library read failures without process termination. Preserves historical findings and does not fabricate missing attestations.

controls.description: Playhead and phrase marker represent the latest step reaching estimated device output, with no queued phrase leaking through view changes.
controls.test: Browser observes independent output timestamps and rendered marker/grid state at 40, 120 and 220 BPM including skips and wrap.

controls.description: Nine real tracks, including dense polyphony, stay sample-aligned under 180ms stalls and CPU throttling. Stop uses a shared 25ms cancellation deadline; rapid restart cannot overlap it or leak visuals.
controls.test: AudioWorklet captures onsets independently of scheduling events; no late starts and <=1 sample skew. Inject a 12ms interruption within stop cancellation and require equal counts/times on every track. The regression failed before the shared deadline fix.

controls.description: Production build boots all five compiled worklets and loads/plays a sample via the bundled manifest.
controls.test: Build and preview browser test; seven extension/engine buttons, exactly one AudioContext and advancing playhead.

controls.description: Permission/read failures give actionable errors and preserve the server and transport.
controls.test: Real HTTP server tests EPERM, failed stream, missing file and valid retry; browser verifies permission feedback.

fixtures: temporary sample library with injected EPERM and stream failure
